clue.text: Which blinding goddess is on a brief holiday? Give up

parts.note: VAC is the short form of vacation, a holiday
Ate is the Greek goddess of folly and ruin, who blinds people to the consequences of their acts

explanation.surface: A question about which goddess of blindness is off on a short break, then an instruction to give up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is on' just puts the goddess after the holiday in the across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacate a post or a room is to relinquish it, i.e. to give it up.

clue.text: Essential compound has energy to squeeze half of tank in

indicators.note: the energy word squeezes the next piece into its middle

parts.note: vim is energy or vigour

indicators.note: the first half of the word tank is taken, its opening two letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A vital substance that gets the energy to cram half a tank into something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to squeeze' and 'in' both look like container signals; only the first is, and the final 'in' simply supplies its own letters at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A vitamin is an organic compound essential in small amounts to the diet.

clue.text: Damage a 15

parts.note: 'what's the damage?' asks what something costs, so damage means cost

explanation.surface: A terse remark that something has damaged a numbered item.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 refers to 15-across, BONE; costa is the anatomical Latin for a rib.
explanation.definitionFit: A costa is a rib, one of the bones of the chest.

clue.text: In growth, I am indebted to 1 down

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters in the words that follow

explanation.surface: A grateful statement that one owes one's growth to a vitamin.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across growTH I AM INdebted; 1 down is VITAMIN, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Thiamin is vitamin B1, one of the B-complex vitamins.

clue.text: Sport short dress (length one's concealed)

indicators.note: the shortened dress hides the length and one inside it
the dress word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a frock is a dress
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Advice to sport a short dress, with a bracketed note that its length is hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: FROCK cut short is FROC; L and I go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport is to play about, and to frolic is to romp playfully.

clue.text: 15 spoke?

definitions.meaning: 15 refers to 15-across, a bone: here the forearm bone on the thumb side
a spoke is a line from centre to rim, as in a wheel or circle

explanation.surface: A two-word puzzle about a bone and a spoke.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a spoke only loosely matches the geometric line from centre to edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The radius is a forearm bone and also the line from a circle's centre to its rim, like a wheel spoke.

clue.text: Tree shelters the very agile

indicators.note: the tree wraps round the other pieces, giving them shelter

parts.note: the lime or linden is a tree
taken as written
so means very, as in 'so good'

explanation.surface: A tree giving shelter to the most nimble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelters' signals a container: the tree surrounds the other two pieces. 'the very agile' reads as a noun phrase, but 'the' and 'very' are both wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithesome is a variant of lithe, meaning supple and nimble.

clue.text: Comfort the panel

definitions.meaning: a control panel, as on a mixing desk or dashboard

explanation.surface: An instruction to comfort a committee or panel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for soothing someone and a noun for a control panel.

clue.text: Catch this! The corrupt member hit hard, as source of gossip

parts.note: a bus is what you catch, so 'catch this' is a playful pointer to one

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or altered, so the letters of the are rearranged

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
to rap is to hit sharply
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A gossip column's tip-off that a corrupt politician has been hit hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' turns THE into HTE. 'Member' wants to be a politician; it is just a leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A bush telegraph is an informal network spreading rumour quickly, so it is a channel of gossip.

clue.text: Mr Redding is on the books

indicators.note: in an across clue, placing one piece on another lets it follow

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the books of the Bible's first part

explanation.surface: Someone named Redding has been registered in the records.
explanation.walkthrough: Otis Redding was the American soul singer of '(Sittin' On) The Dock of the Bay'.
explanation.definitionFit: Otis was the first name of the soul singer Redding, so Mr Redding is a first-name reference.

clue.text: Primarily incestuous practice of having sisters as girlfriends, possibly overwhelming

indicators.note: primarily points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.words: practice of having sisters as girlfriends
parts.note: sisters are nuns, so going out with them would be 'nun dating'

explanation.surface: A lurid tale of incest and sisters as girlfriends, perhaps overwhelming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' flags the invented phrase NUN DATING; 'sisters' are religious sisters, not siblings.
explanation.definitionFit: Inundating means flooding, and so swamping or overwhelming someone.

clue.text: Preserve to some degree penetrating wood

indicators.note: the degree goes into the wood, entering it

parts.note: elm is a wood
an MBA is a degree, Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: Wood treated with preservative that soaks some way into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to some degree' reads as 'partly', but 'some degree' is a named qualification and 'penetrating' puts it inside the wood.
explanation.definitionFit: To embalm a corpse is to preserve it from decay.

clue.text: Spend little time in ring and might one get slated?

indicators.note: use and time are placed in the ring

parts.note: a hoop is a ring
to spend is to use up
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A boxer who spends little time in the ring wondering if he'll be criticised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slated' looks like 'criticised'; a housetop is roofed with slates.
explanation.definitionFit: A housetop is the roof of a house, which may well be covered with slates.

clue.text: Delighted women's liberation doubly evident in advert seeking buxom lady?

indicators.note: two Ws are freed from the advert, so both are removed

parts.note: a classified ad reading 'wench wanted', a wench being a buxom lass
W is the abbreviation for women, here taken twice

explanation.surface: A delighted feminist spots an advertisement for a buxom woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking both Ws from WENCH WANTED leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enchanted is to be charmed, delighted.

clue.text: Mixture of soil and earth for plant

indicators.note: a mixture blends the letters of soil and earth into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener's recipe of soil and earth for growing a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Horsetail, Equisetum, is a rush-like plant.

clue.text: What's to contend with the 1 down 3?

definitions.meaning: a '... of contention' is the thing argued over
1 down 3 is vitamin thiamin, also called vitamin B1

explanation.surface: A question about what must be battled alongside a vitamin.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 down is VITAMIN and 3 down THIAMIN, also known as B1; read B1 as B plus ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'bone of contention' names the subject of a dispute, and B1 written out spells the word.

clue.text: Port — what's between you and drinking it?

definitions.meaning: A port city in the south of Ireland

definitions.text: what's between you and drinking it?
definitions.meaning: a bottle stopper stands between you and the wine inside

explanation.surface: A question about what stops you drinking port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the fortified wine, but it is an Irish harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Cork is an Irish port, and a cork is the stopper you must pull before drinking.

clue.text: Miss features in prize photo

indicators.note: the losing word appears inside the prize word

parts.note: a cup is a prize, as in a trophy
to miss is to lose, e.g. a chance

explanation.surface: A beauty queen appears in a prize-winning photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' wants to be a beauty queen featuring in a photo; it is the verb, and 'features in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-up is a photograph taken at close range.

clue.text: Bloody savage strangles river bird

parts.note: red is the colour of blood

indicators.note: the savage holds the river tight inside it

parts.note: a beast is a savage creature

explanation.surface: A bloodthirsty brute throttles a bird by the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Redbreast is another name for the robin, a bird.

clue.text: Oyster, perhaps, one born up against how it's eaten heartlessly?

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
V for versus, meaning against

indicators.note: the word loses its central letter

parts.note: oysters are eaten alive

explanation.surface: A question on whether an oyster is eaten with no heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IB into BI; 'heartlessly' removes the middle I of ALIVE, leaving ALVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster is one example of a bivalve, a mollusc with a two-part hinged shell.

clue.text: Front 15 I'm not sure under back

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece goes below the first

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship
um is a hesitation noise

explanation.surface: Someone hesitating over a front-facing bone at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 refers to 15-across, BONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the breastbone at the front of the chest.

clue.text: African capital has no name for the crowned heavyweight champion?

indicators.note: the name letter is taken away

parts.note: Muhammad Ali, heavyweight champion, crowned and so 'King Ali'

explanation.surface: An African capital lacks a name for the boxing champion.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing N from KING ALI leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Kigali is the capital city of Rwanda in central Africa.

clue.text: Nellie or Rocky has fewer friends?

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Asks whether Nellie or Rocky has fewer friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' looks like a name; it is the anagram signal for NELLIE OR.
explanation.definitionFit: To be lonelier is to be more isolated, i.e. more friendless.

clue.text: Schooner as both glass and ship?

definitions.text: Schooner as both glass and ship?

parts.words: Schooner as both glass and ship?
parts.note: a schooner is both a large glass and a sailing ship, and one word covers both senses

explanation.surface: Wondering if a schooner is both a drinking glass and a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is both a container for liquid and a ship.

clue.text: 15 in 22, say

indicators.note: 'say' signals a word spoken aloud

parts.note: 22 refers to 22-across, a vessel; a scull is a small rowing boat

explanation.surface: A cross-reference saying 15 in 22.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is 15-across, BONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull is the bony case of the head.

clue.text: Tin, say, containing a fish 15

indicators.note: the metal holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: tin is an example of a metal
carp is a fish

explanation.surface: A tin can containing fish and a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' signals the metal surrounding the fish piece; 'Tin, say' is an example definition of the outer word, not tinned food.
explanation.definitionFit: A metacarpal is one of the bones of the hand.

clue.text: 15 found in Dublin Bay every so often

indicators.note: every other letter of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A bone discovered on the shore of Dublin Bay.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the even letters of Dublin Bay.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is a forearm bone on the little finger side.

clue.text: Quiet singer's 15

parts.note: P is piano, quiet in music
Elvis Presley, the singer

explanation.surface: A quiet singer's bone.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a possessive that adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelvis is the bony basin at the base of the spine.

clue.text: Hit on plot, which is chaotic

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting one piece on another puts it after

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
to lam is to thrash or hit

explanation.surface: A gardener hits on a plot, which is chaotic.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam is utter confusion, an uproar or scene of chaos.
